scope_line: Scope: the hermes-agent repository (agent loop, tools, skills, curator, approvals, gateway, MCP and ACP servers, desktop and web, CI) plus the first-party hermes-agent-self-evolution repository (DSPy and GEPA skill optimisation). Nous Portal and hosted services are out of scope.

A1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

A2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

A3.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B3.evidence: Typed tool schemas (model_tools.py, toolsets.py) served over MCP (mcp_serve.py) and the Agent Client Protocol (acp_adapter); no OpenAPI description of the serve API and no dry-run.

C1.evidence: CLI, TUI, desktop and web layouts are code; persona text (SOUL.md) is data but is not layout.

C2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD views (fixed per-archetype rule).

C3.evidence: UI strings externalised in locales/ and translated READMEs; themes are engineer-managed.

D1.evidence: Cron jobs are defined in natural language or the CLI and run agent tasks on schedules (cron/); plugin hooks add behaviour; there is no general condition and action engine.

D2.evidence: Gateway adapters receive platform and webhook events; the MCP server lets clients poll live events (mcp_serve.py); no retry or replay for outbound subscribers.

D3.evidence: Plugins register hooks that run in-process without a sandbox (plugins/); the agent's own commands can run in Docker, SSH or remote sandbox backends with guards (tools/terminal_tool_backends.py, terminal_tool_guards.py).

E1.evidence: No automated accessibility scanning found for the TUI, desktop or web interfaces.

E2.evidence: Every skill mutation by any actor is appended to a JSONL ledger with content-addressed before and after snapshots (tools/skill_ledger.py); staged approvals are recorded; sessions are stored in SQLite. Configuration and memory changes are not in the ledger.
E2.alt_note: Skills are the main definition surface and are fully audited with approvals.

E3.evidence: Session export and import (hermes_state_portability.py) and user-editable memory files; data stays on the user's machine; not driven by tags.

E4.evidence: Command scanning with tirith and dangerous-command approvals with an LLM risk classifier and floors (tools/approval_smart.py, approval_floors.py); skill security scans and AST audits before install or write (tools/skills_guard.py, skills_ast_audit.py); OSV and supply-chain scans in CI (.github/workflows/osv-scanner.yml, supply-chain-audit.yml).

F1.evidence: Skills, the agent's main customisation surface, have a per-mutation ledger with single-edit rollback that fails closed (tools/skill_ledger.py); curator archives are recoverable with hermes curator restore; a write blocked by the security scan restores the original automatically (tools/skill_manager_tool.py:353-461).
F1.alt_note: Ledger entries are addressable and rollback is automatic on failed scans; links to evidence are partial.

F2.evidence: By default, skill and memory writes apply directly and are ledgered. With skills.write_approval or memory.write_approval on, writes are staged with a gist and applied through /skills approve (tools/write_approval.py:73-189); the self-evolution repo proposes evaluated skill variants as pull requests.

F3.evidence: By default only protected instruction files always need a human (cli-config.yaml.example:573-576); skill and memory gates default to off (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:1320). With them on, each change class has its own gate.

F4.evidence: Numbered configuration migrations run on update (hermes_cli/config_migrations.py:379-397); bundled-skill sync updates shipped skills without overwriting user copies (tools/skills_sync*.py); skills follow the agentskills.io specification.

G1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic-store query performance (fixed per-archetype rule).

G2.evidence: Single user per installation with isolated profiles (separate homes); no multi-tenant limits.

G3.evidence: evals/ holds regression probes named after failures found in use (for example auxiliary_resource_exhausted.py, cron_error_diagnostics.py): ceilings are discovered in incidents.

H1.evidence: Python agent, gateway, desktop, web and sandbox images are separate artifacts built from one repository (Dockerfile, .github/workflows/sandbox-image.yml, desktop-bundled-release.yml).

H2.evidence: Import guards in CI (.github/workflows/lazy-deps-guard.yml, case-collision-check.yml); no architectural boundary lint.

H3.evidence: Python, JavaScript and Rust tests, lint, Nix, OSV, supply-chain, desktop E2E and install E2E run in CI with no draft filter (.github/workflows/tests.yml, js-tests.yml, rust-tests.yml, e2e-desktop.yml); no accessibility check.
H3.alt_note: Every change class except accessibility is checked.

I1.evidence: Declarative skills (SKILL.md), Python plugins with hooks, MCP servers, providers and a plugin catalogue with hundreds of entries (plugin-catalog/, skills/, optional-skills/, optional-mcps/).
I1.alt_note: A versioned registry and hub exist.

I2.evidence: Hub skills are scanned and installed only after confirmation (tools/skills_hub_install.py, skills_guard.py); plugins run with full trust; commands can be sent to sandbox backends.
I2.alt_note: Scanned skills plus sandboxed command backends isolate most third-party and AI-written code.

I3.evidence: Skill linter (tools/skill_linter.py), curator dry-run (hermes curator run --dry-run), logs (hermes_logging.py) and local iteration against the user's own profile.

K1.evidence: MCP server exposing conversation, messaging, event and approval tools (mcp_serve.py) and an ACP adapter for editors (acp_adapter/); typed tool registry (model_tools.py).
K1.alt_note: The MCP surface covers messaging, not the full capability set.

K2.evidence: Users complete tasks conversationally across CLI, desktop and messaging platforms with tool actions; users author skills, memory and cron jobs in natural language, with staged approvals as preview when enabled; evaluation probes (evals/) and GEPA evaluation datasets.
K2.alt_note: Almost every capability is reachable conversationally.

K3.evidence: Dangerous-command approvals with LLM risk classification and floors, tirith scanning, sandbox backends, subagent auto-deny and session audit; commands otherwise run with the user's ambient authority; no idempotency keys.
K3.alt_note: Per-action risk classification and approval previews are level 3 and 4 features.

N1.evidence: One provider layer maps many model vendors onto a canonical chat interface (providers/, agent/*_adapter.py), and one gateway maps Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp and other platforms onto a canonical conversation model (gateway/).

N2.evidence: Plugin catalogue entries, provider adapters, platform adapters and MCP servers cover auth, messaging and lifecycle; skill hub sources include official, GitHub, ClawHub and skills.sh (tools/skills_hub_*.py).

N3.evidence: Standard protocols (MCP, ACP, OpenAI-compatible APIs) and versioned configuration; no deprecation windows.

O1.evidence: Kernel of sessions (conversation), gateway platforms (channel), profiles (identity), approvals (permission), cron and delegation (workflow), and skills and files (content); no domain nouns.

O2.evidence: Many domains ship as skill bundles on an unchanged kernel (skills/, optional-skills/), and the agent creates new domain skills itself.
O2.alt_note: If skills are judged too small to count as domains.

O3.evidence: Skills are versionable, installable bundles under the agentskills.io specification, installed from the hub with scanning and synced on update.
O3.alt_note: Bundles are composable (curator umbrella skills), upgradeable and AI-assembled.

J1.evidence: The session database with full-text search is available to the agent in real time (hermes_state_fts.py, hermes_state_search.py); every skill gets view, use and patch counts automatically (tools/skill_usage.py).
J1.alt_note: Per-definition instrumentation is added automatically for every skill.

J2.evidence: Every skill has view, use and patch counts linked to it (tools/skill_usage.py), and the curator triages skills into active, stale and archived (website/docs/user-guide/features/curator.md).
J2.alt_note: Usage counts are not versioned per skill revision.

J3.evidence: Session search over the agent's own history; the self-evolution repo builds evaluation datasets from Hermes, Claude Code and Copilot session histories (README, --eval-source sessiondb). No continuous mining in the product.

M1.evidence: After each turn a background fork proposes skill and memory updates grounded in the conversation (agent/background_review.py); GEPA ranks skill variants on a Pareto front with evaluation evidence (self-evolution repo). Covers skills only.
M1.alt_note: Ranked, evidence-backed proposals with expected impact exist for the agent's main behaviour surface.

M3.evidence: The background review is an autonomous authoring lane that applies skill and memory changes every turn (agent/background_review.py); GEPA improvements reach every user through upstream pull requests.
M3.alt_note: The cross-user path depends on an offline companion tool.

M4.evidence: The curator keeps, marks stale or archives skills from measured usage over fixed windows (14 and 30 days, website/docs/user-guide/features/curator.md); GEPA compares variants against the baseline skill before proposing. Nothing measures the outcome of an applied skill in use.
M4.alt_note: The curator records a metric, window and explicit keep or archive decision per skill.

L1.evidence: Version reporting and state health checks (hermes_state_health.py) and a configuration display; no machine-readable deployed-configuration endpoint.

L2.evidence: Nix flake and lock files reproduce the environment (flake.nix, uv.lock); install E2E jobs build fresh environments per run.
L2.alt_note: Reproducible environments are built per change in CI.

L3.evidence: Behaviour probes (evals/), desktop and install E2E suites; no changed-path map or adoption instrumentation at ship.

P1.evidence: background_review is enabled by default (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py:814): after turns, a forked agent decides whether to save or update skills and memory (agent/background_review.py).
P1.alt_note: The curator's consolidation learns which skills stick, but only when enabled.

P2.evidence: Skill writes pass security scans, AST audits and a linter (tools/skills_guard.py, skills_ast_audit.py, skill_linter.py). The first-party GEPA optimiser evaluates variants against the baseline skill before proposing, when it is run (hermes-agent-self-evolution README).

limits: Repository evidence only. The self-evolution repository's last commit is 2026-06-17, and only phase 1 (skills) is implemented; phases 2 and 3 were not scored. No live runs were performed, so the effects of background review and the curator are read from code and documentation. Single rater.
reading: **Strongest:** Learning (2.5), the highest point estimate in the sample, though its range (2.3–3.1) overlaps OpenClaw and PostHog. Background review is on by default and turns conversations into skill and memory changes (P1 3). Every skill has usage signals and curator triage (J2 3). Every change is ledgered with rollback (F1 3). **Gaps by default:** skill and memory approval gates are off (F3 2), and learned skills get security and lint checks but no baseline evaluation (P2 2). **With opt-ins** (write approval on, the GEPA optimiser run), Hermes is the only system in the sample that passes every closed-loop stage.
